subject: Model-fit intake: sensitive prompt samples + next steps
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@curamind.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@curamind.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-12T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Model-fit intake: sensitive prompt samples + next steps

Hi Elena and Samir — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can scope an eval and pilot: 

Call recap (30m):
- Primary use case: anonymized triage + suggested routing for clinical intake forms (short free-text patient notes).
- Key constraints: PHI must be redacted before leaving your network; certain entities (SSN, full names) are never shareable.
- Success signals: 95% intent-class accuracy on triage labels, <2% hallucination rate on extracted ICD suggestions.

Redwood model recommendations (initial):
- Redwood-13B-v2 (fp16) — good balance of accuracy / latency for batch evals.
- Redwood-7B-8bit (fast) — cost-efficient baseline for throughput-sensitive paths.
- Fallback: Redwood-3B-quant (low-latency, lower cost) for routing-only endpoints.

What we need from you: 
1) A prioritized set of ~200 real-world prompts (anonymized) covering: typical intake, ambiguous entries, and edge cases (abbreviations, partial sentences, mixed language). Use the attached prompt_template.csv to format samples.
2) Mark the top 20 edge cases you fear most (safety/regulatory or model brittleness).
3) A short doc listing redaction rules we must enforce (we can consume redacted examples).

Security & transfer: For anything marked sensitive, please upload to the secure intake link (we will provide a presigned S3 link) or share via your preferred SFTP. Do not email raw PHI.

Attachments: call-recording-20280812.mp3 (recording), prompt_template.csv (CSV template), redaction-guidance.md (our suggested starter).

Proposed timeline: 
- You share first batch (50 anonymized prompts + edge case notes) by EOD 2028-08-18.
- Redwood completes an initial evaluation (models above) and shares benchmark links by 2028-08-24.

Owners: Avery (pilot coordination), Marissa (eval & benchmarks), Neha (security & redaction checks).

If that works, we’ll send the secure upload instructions and a short Slack channel invite for day-to-day coordination.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Model-fit intake: sensitive prompt samples + next steps

Hi Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround. Short answers to your questions and a couple of links you can expect in the benchmark deck: 

Benchmarks we’ll publish (initial evaluation):
- Intent accuracy (macro) on triage labels
- Precision/recall on extraction tasks (ICD suggestion sampling)
- Hallucination rate (manual spot checks + automated divergence metric)
- Latency P50/P95 for single-request and batch throughput
- Cost per 1k tokens across model variants

How we’ll use your prompts:
- We’ll use the 50 you provide as a held-out eval set. If you provide a larger corpus we’ll split by case (80/20) and keep the eval set stable across model runs.

Redaction checklist (starter):
- Remove names, full addresses, SSNs, MRN numbers — replace with <NAME>, <ADDRESS>, <SSN>, <MRN>.
- If dates are core to the case, shift by a consistent offset (e.g., minus 2 years) rather than removing.
- Mask any free-text clinician notes that include direct patient identifiers; keep clinical content (symptoms, diagnoses) intact.

Next steps I’ll take this week:
- Prepare the Redwood Console benchmark view for 'CuraMind pilot' and share a read-only link (one-click) so your PMs can follow progress.
- Assemble a minimal eval script and Docker image so you can reproduce runs locally if desired.

We’ll also enumerate the top 20 edge cases (formatting, abbreviations, mixed-language snippets) once we see the first batch — that will help tune tokenization/normalization.

Marissa Cole
Senior Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
